claims.text: The rapid growth of algorithmic fairness research has led to inconsistent motivations, terminology, and notation across the literature.
Implicit choices and assumptions made to justify prediction-based decision-making can give rise to fairness concerns.
Fairness definitions across existing literature can be organized into a notationally consistent catalog.

evidence.description: The authors state that the rapid growth of this new field has led to wildly inconsistent motivations, terminology, and notation, presenting a serious challenge for cataloging and comparing definitions.
The authors explicate the choices and assumptions made to justify prediction-based decision-making and show how they can raise fairness concerns.
The paper presents a notationally consistent catalog of fairness definitions from the literature.

methodologies.name: Taxonomic Conceptual Synthesis
methodologies.description: Explicates implicit choices and assumptions in prediction-based decision-making and systematizes existing fairness definitions using standardized mathematical notation.

limitations.text: Inconsistent motivations, terminology, and notation across prior algorithmic fairness literature present a serious challenge for cataloging and comparing fairness definitions.
